symbols.name: input length
symbols.meaning: The number of cells that hold the input, which is the argument of the running time cost.
symbols.quote: The running time cost of a machine is the number of steps it takes on an input, as a worst-case function of $n$, the number of cells that hold the input.

symbols.name: exponent constant
symbols.meaning: The fixed constant $2^{-182}$ in the exponent of the bound $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$.
symbols.quote: Here $\kappa = 2^{-182}$ is a fixed constant of the theorem, and its running time is $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$.

symbols.name: machine
symbols.meaning: A machine whose running time cost is being measured.
symbols.quote: For a machine $A$ and an input length $n$, the running time cost is $T_A(n)$, the largest number of steps $A$ takes on any input of length $n$.

symbols.name: running time cost
symbols.meaning: The largest number of steps machine $A$ takes on any input of length $n$.
symbols.quote: For a machine $A$ and an input length $n$, the running time cost is $T_A(n)$, the largest number of steps $A$ takes on any input of length $n$.

symbols.name: example machine
symbols.meaning: The example machine that reads cells from the first cell until it finds a $1$ or reaches the last cell.
symbols.quote: Take the machine $M$ that starts on the first cell.
